chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Mu'allā (husband who delays consummation) when he is compelled (to choose) and does not return (to consummation), he is divorced with a final divorce.

key_terms.الْمُؤَلَّى: The Mu'allā, a husband granted a four-month period to consummate marriage or be divorced
key_terms.بَائِنَةً: Final/Irrevocable (referring to the type of divorce)
key_terms.وُقِفَ: He was compelled or stood at the point of decision

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Mu'allā fails to consummate the marriage after the four-month period?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the specific legal consequence when a Mu'allā, after being compelled to choose between consummation or divorce, fails to return, resulting in a 'talaq ba'inah' (irrevocable divorce). This ruling distinguishes the scenario from a simple revocable divorce, emphasizing the finality of the bond unless a new contract is executed, a point of significant discussion among Shia jurists regarding the conditions of 'ilā' and 'liʿān'.
